people.name: Titus Larcius
people.summary: Consul 501 and 498 and, according to Livy, the first Roman dictator (501), appointed against a Latin threat and the Sabines, with Sp. Cassius as master of horse.
people.detail: Livy admits his sources disagreed on whether Larcius or M'. Valerius was the first dictator. Dionysius gives a long account of a census held under his dictatorship. The Larcii were an Etruscan-named gens that vanished from the Fasti after the early 5th century.

people.name: Manius Valerius Maximus
people.summary: Popular dictator of 494 who won the plebs' trust by protecting debtors during the levy, triumphed over the Sabines, and resigned rather than break his promises when the Senate refused debt relief.
people.detail: He is presented as a Valerian friend of the people, part of the family tradition that runs from Publicola to the consuls of 449 and 300. The title Maximus was said to have been granted for his conduct.

people.name: Attius Tullius
people.summary: Chief of the Volsci at Antium who received the exiled Coriolanus and led the Volscian war against Rome of 488; Plutarch calls him Tullus Aufidius, the name Shakespeare used.
people.detail: Livy makes him engineer the expulsion of Volscians from the Roman games of 490 to provoke war. After Coriolanus withdrew, the Volsci quarrelled with the Aequi and Attius disappears from the record.

people.name: Anaxilas
people.fullName: Anaxilas son of Cretines, tyrant of Rhegium
people.summary: Tyrant of Rhegium c. 494-476 of Messenian descent, who seized Zancle across the Strait and renamed it Messana, controlling both shores; ally of Terillus of Himera and father-in-law of Hiero of Syracuse.
people.detail: His coins show a hare and a mule-car commemorating his Olympic mule-cart victory. He blocked the Strait against Etruscan shipping. His sons were displaced by his regent Micythus, who led the Rhegines in the disaster against the Iapygians in 473.

people.name: Theron
people.fullName: Theron son of Aenesidamus, tyrant of Acragas
people.summary: Tyrant of Acragas c. 488-472, Gelon's father-in-law and partner at Himera (480), whose expulsion of Terillus from Himera provoked the Carthaginian invasion; he used Carthaginian prisoners to build the Olympieion.
people.detail: Pindar celebrated his Olympic chariot victory of 476 (Olympian 2 and 3), with its unusual eschatology of the Isles of the Blest. His son Thrasydaeus lost power soon after his death.

people.name: Caeso Fabius
people.summary: Consul 484, 481 and 479, the most prominent of the three Fabian brothers; after first opposing agrarian reform he proposed distributing conquered land, then led his gens to private war against Veii and died with the 306 Fabii at the Cremera (477).
people.detail: Livy places Caeso at the head of the clan's march out through the right arch of the Porta Carmentalis, ever after ill-omened. Dionysius makes him prosecutor of Sp. Cassius.
people.death: killed with the Fabii at the Cremera

people.name: Marcus Fabius
people.summary: Consul 483 and 480, who won the bloody battle before Veii in 480 but refused the triumph because his brother Quintus and his colleague Cn. Manlius had fallen; he joined the Cremera expedition.
people.detail: His care for wounded soldiers in patrician houses is Livy's turning point in Fabian popularity.

people.name: Veturia
people.summary: Mother of Cn. Marcius Coriolanus who, at the head of the Roman matrons, went to his camp at the Fossae Cluiliae and shamed him into withdrawing the Volscian army; Plutarch calls her Volumnia.
people.detail: Livy gives her one of the great speeches of his first decade: 'Am I in your camp as a mother or a prisoner?'. Her deed was commemorated in the temple of Fortuna Muliebris. She is the model of the Roman mother whose authority over an adult son outweighs his military command.

people.name: Volumnia
people.summary: Wife of Coriolanus (Vergilia in Plutarch) who went with Veturia and her children to his camp in 488; she appears in Livy holding their two small sons.
people.detail: The naming differs between Livy (wife Volumnia) and Plutarch (mother Volumnia, wife Vergilia), and Shakespeare followed Plutarch.

people.name: Valeria
people.fullName: Valeria, sister of P. Valerius Publicola
people.summary: Sister of Publicola who, according to Dionysius and Plutarch, proposed that the matrons go to Coriolanus' camp and became the first priestess of Fortuna Muliebris.
people.detail: Her role belongs to the Valerian family tradition, which inserted Valerii into the key moments of early Republican history.

people.name: Gnaeus Genucius
people.summary: Tribune of the plebs in 473 who indicted the consuls of 474 for failing to implement the agrarian law and was found dead in his house on the day of the trial.
people.detail: The Genucii were a leading plebeian family: L. Genucius was the first plebeian consul to lead an army under his own auspices (362), and a tribune Genucius carried the laws of 342.
people.death: found dead in his home, presumed murdered

people.name: Gaius Terentilius Harsa
people.summary: Tribune of the plebs in 462 whose bill for a commission to define and limit consular imperium began the decade-long campaign for written law that produced the Twelve Tables.

people.name: Caeso Quinctius
people.summary: Son of Cincinnatus, a giant and orator who led young patricians in driving tribunes from the Forum; accused of causing a plebeian's death, he jumped bail and fled to Etruria in 461, ruining his father.
people.detail: His case gives the first recorded use of sureties (vades) for a defendant's appearance. The witness against him, M. Volscius Fictor, was later convicted of perjury.

people.name: Ducetius
people.summary: Hellenised Sicel leader who in the 450s united the native towns of eastern Sicily, founded Menaenum and Palike, fought Syracuse and Acragas, and after defeat and exile at Corinth returned to found Kale Akte; he died in 440.
people.detail: His career, known from Diodorus, is the most ambitious native response to Greek colonisation in Sicily.

people.name: Lucius Siccius Dentatus
people.summary: Legendary plebeian soldier, the 'Roman Achilles', credited with 120 battles, 45 frontal wounds, eight single combats, 14 civic crowns and many other decorations; murdered on the decemvirs' orders in 449.
people.detail: Tribune of the plebs in 454 in some accounts, he was a symbol of plebeian service to the state. His catalogue of dona militaria is the classic list for Roman military decorations.
people.death: killed by soldiers sent with him by the decemvirs

people.name: Lucius Valerius Potitus
people.summary: Leader with M. Horatius of the senatorial opposition to the decemvirs, consul 449, who carried the leges Valeriae Horatiae and defeated the Aequi and Volsci, triumphing by vote of the people.

people.name: Marcus Horatius Barbatus
people.summary: Consul 449 with L. Valerius, co-author of the leges Valeriae Horatiae restoring provocatio and tribunician sacrosanctity, and victor over the Sabines.

people.name: Lucius Icilius
people.summary: Tribune of the plebs 456, who carried the law distributing the Aventine to the plebs, betrothed of Verginia in 449, and again tribune in 449, when he carried the popular vote granting triumphs to Valerius and Horatius.
people.detail: The Icilii appear as hereditary champions of the plebs in Livy's narrative.

people.name: Lucius Verginius
people.summary: Plebeian centurion who killed his daughter Verginia in the Forum with a butcher's knife rather than let Appius Claudius claim her as a slave, roused the army to secession, and as tribune of the plebs (449) prosecuted Appius.

people.name: Lucius Papirius Mugillanus
people.summary: Suffect consul 444 with L. Sempronius Atratinus after the first consular tribunes abdicated, and with him the first censors (443); his name in the treaty with Ardea and the linen books was cited by Licinius Macer.

people.name: Mamercus Aemilius Mamercinus
people.summary: Three times dictator (437, 434, 426) and consular tribune, victor over Veii and Fidenae, author of the law limiting the censorship to eighteen months, for which the censors degraded him to the status of aerarius.
people.detail: He took Fidenae in 426 by mining under its citadel, according to Livy. His dignity under the censors' punishment became exemplary.

people.name: Aulus Postumius Tubertus
people.summary: Dictator 431 who defeated the Aequi and Volsci at Mount Algidus; a story, rejected by Livy, said he executed his son for leaving his post, the 'imperia Postumiana'.

people.name: Hermocrates
people.summary: Syracusan aristocrat who at the Congress of Gela (424) urged 'Sicily for the Sicilians', organised resistance to the Athenian expedition (415-413), led a Syracusan squadron in the Aegean, and was killed in 407 trying to force his way back into Syracuse.
people.detail: Thucydides gives him two major speeches. His daughter married Dionysius I, who exploited his memory.

people.name: Postumia
people.summary: Vestal tried for unchastity in 420 on the grounds of her elegant dress and free speech, acquitted, and told by the pontifex maximus to dress more soberly.

people.name: Velthur Spurinna
people.summary: Tarquinian magistrate honoured in the Elogia Tarquiniensia as the first Etruscan to lead an army across the sea to Sicily, probably in support of Athens against Syracuse (414-413).
people.detail: The elogia were set up in the 1st century AD by his descendants; the haruspex Spurinna who warned Caesar about the Ides of March may belong to the same family.

people.name: Hannibal son of Gisco (409)
people.fullName: Hannibal son of Gisco, grandson of Hamilcar the Magonid
people.summary: Carthaginian general who led the great invasion of Sicily in 409, destroying Selinus and Himera, and died of plague while besieging Acragas in 406.
people.detail: He sacrificed 3,000 Himeraean prisoners to the shade of his grandfather Hamilcar, killed at Himera in 480. Not to be confused with the Hannibal son of Gisco of the First Punic War.

people.name: Himilco
people.summary: Carthaginian general who completed the sack of Acragas (406), took Gela, made the treaty of 405 with Dionysius, destroyed Messana and besieged Syracuse (396), where plague ruined his army; he bribed his way out and killed himself at Carthage.
people.death: suicide by starvation after the disaster at Syracuse

people.name: Dionysius II
people.summary: Tyrant of Syracuse 367-357 and 346-344, son of Dionysius I by the Locrian Doris; Plato tried to make him a philosopher-king; expelled by Dion, he ruled Locri, returned to Syracuse, and surrendered Ortygia to Timoleon, ending his days in Corinth.
people.detail: Anecdotes made him a schoolmaster or begging priest at Corinth, a proverbial example of fallen fortune.

people.name: Dion

roles.t: General with full powers of Syracuse

people.summary: Brother-in-law of Dionysius I and disciple of Plato, who brought Plato to Syracuse, was exiled by Dionysius II, returned with a small mercenary force in 357 to liberate the city, and was murdered by Callippus in 354.

people.name: Hicetas
people.summary: Syracusan exile and tyrant of Leontini who invited Corinthian help against Dionysius II and then allied with Carthage against Timoleon; defeated at Adranum and later captured and executed with his family.

people.name: Archidamus III
people.summary: Eurypontid king of Sparta (360-338), son of Agesilaus, who led mercenaries to Italy at Tarentum's request and was killed by the Messapians and Lucanians at Manduria in 338.

people.name: Lucius Manlius Imperiosus
people.summary: Dictator 363 to drive the ceremonial nail against plague, who tried to raise an army and was forced to resign; prosecuted in 362 for harshness, he was saved when his son Titus (later Torquatus) forced the prosecutor to drop the case.

people.name: Marcus Popillius Laenas
people.summary: Plebeian consul four times (359, 356, 350, 348), who defeated the Tiburtines and in 350 the Gauls, fighting wounded in the front line; ancestor of the Popillii Laenates.
people.detail: As consul in 359 he was also flamen Carmentalis and, by tradition, came straight from a sacrifice in his priestly robe to calm a riot.

people.name: Lucius Furius Camillus
people.summary: Grandson (or son) of the great Camillus; dictator 350 and 345, consul 349, when his military tribune Valerius Corvus fought the Gallic champion; he vowed the temple of Juno Moneta during the Auruncan war of 345.

people.name: Brutulus Papius
people.summary: Powerful Samnite noble blamed by his people for breaking the truce with Rome; he killed himself in 322 before he could be surrendered, and the Samnites sent his body to Rome.

people.name: Gaius Junius Bubulcus
people.summary: Plebeian consul 317, 313 and 311, censor 307 and dictator 302, who campaigned in Samnium and Apulia, vowed the temple of Salus in 311 and dedicated it as dictator in 302.
people.detail: As censor with M. Valerius Maximus he built roads through the countryside at public expense.

people.name: Hamilcar son of Gisco
people.summary: Carthaginian general who defeated Agathocles at the Himeras (311) and besieged Syracuse, but was captured in a failed night assault in 309 and executed; his head was sent to Agathocles in Africa.
people.death: captured and killed by the Syracusans

people.name: Ophellas
people.summary: Macedonian officer of Alexander, governor of Cyrene for Ptolemy and then independent, who marched an army and colonists across the Syrtis to join Agathocles against Carthage and was murdered by him in 308.

people.name: Bomilcar
people.summary: Carthaginian general who, during Agathocles' invasion, attempted to make himself tyrant of Carthage in 308; defeated in street fighting, he was crucified in the agora.

people.name: Archagathus
people.summary: Elder son of Agathocles, left in command in Africa; defeated in the interior and abandoned by his father in 307, he was killed by the mutinous army.

people.name: Gaius Fabius Pictor
people.summary: Patrician who painted the walls of the temple of Salus (dedicated 302) and was the first Roman noble known as a painter, giving his branch of the Fabii the cognomen Pictor; grandfather of the historian Q. Fabius Pictor.

people.name: Lucius Volumnius Flamma
people.summary: Plebeian consul 307 and 296, colleague of Appius Claudius Caecus both times; in 296 he defeated Samnite raiders on the Volturnus, and his patrician wife Verginia founded the cult of Plebeian Chastity.

people.name: Marcus Atilius Regulus (cos. 294)
people.summary: Plebeian consul 294 who, his camp attacked near Luceria, vowed a temple to Jupiter Stator and defeated the Samnites; probably father of the Regulus of the First Punic War.

people.name: Spurius Carvilius Maximus
people.summary: Plebeian consul 293 and 272, who took Cominium while Papirius won at Aquilonia, cast a colossal Jupiter for the Capitol from Samnite armour and built the temple of Fors Fortuna; in 272 he completed the Samnite war.

people.name: Publius Cornelius Rufinus
people.summary: Consul 290 and 277 and dictator, who was beaten in the Cranita hills but took Croton by a ruse; in 275 the censor Fabricius expelled him from the Senate for owning ten pounds of silver plate. Ancestor of Sulla.

people.name: Decius Vibellius

roles.t: Commander of the garrison of Rhegium

people.summary: Commander of the Campanian legion of 4,000 placed in Rhegium by Rome in 282, who in 280 massacred or expelled the citizens and held the city until Rome retook it in 270; he went blind and killed himself.

people.name: Lucius Aemilius Barbula
people.summary: Consul 281 who led the first Roman campaign against Tarentum, ravaging its territory and withdrawing before Pyrrhus' vanguard, and triumphed in 280 over the Tarentines, Samnites and Sallentini.

people.name: Milo

roles.t: Commander of the garrison of Tarentum

people.summary: Pyrrhus' trusted general who led the advance guard to Tarentum in 281, commanded the city's garrison, and in 272 surrendered the citadel to the Romans in exchange for safe passage.

people.name: Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus Maximus
people.fullName: Gnaeus Domitius Cn. f. Calvinus Maximus
people.summary: Plebeian consul 283, dictator 280 for holding elections, and the first plebeian censor to complete the lustrum (280); founder of the Domitii who later produced the Ahenobarbi and the emperor Nero.

people.name: Marcus Fulvius Flaccus (cos. 264)
people.summary: Plebeian consul 264 who completed the destruction of Volsinii, brought its god Vortumnus to Rome, and triumphed; his colleague Appius Claudius Caudex led the first army to Sicily.

people.name: Fabia
people.fullName: Fabia, younger daughter of M. Fabius Ambustus
people.summary: Patrician wife of the plebeian C. Licinius Stolo whose envy of her sister, married to a consular tribune, Livy makes the spark of the Licinio-Sextian agitation.

people.name: Spurius Lucretius
people.summary: Father of Lucretia, prefect of the city under Tarquin, who joined the conspiracy of Brutus, was elected suffect consul in 509 after Collatinus' resignation and died in office within days.

people.name: Marcus Horatius Pulvillus
people.summary: Suffect consul 509 and consul 507, who dedicated the Capitoline temple; told during the ceremony that his son had died, he finished the dedication with his hand on the doorpost. Polybius' treaty with Carthage names him with Brutus.

people.name: Titus Herminius
people.summary: One of the two companions of Horatius Cocles at the bridge (508), consul 506, killed fighting at Lake Regillus (496); the Herminii, of Etruscan name, vanish after the mid-5th century.

people.name: Sextus Tarquinius
people.summary: Son of Tarquinius Superbus who took Gabii by treachery and whose rape of Lucretia provoked the expulsion of the kings; he fled to Gabii and was killed there in revenge.

people.name: Arruns Tarquinius
people.summary: Son of Tarquinius Superbus who, at the Silva Arsia in 509, charged the consul Brutus; the two killed each other.
people.death: killed in single combat with Brutus

people.name: Arruns Porsenna
people.summary: Son of Porsenna who led a Clusine army against Aricia and was defeated and killed by the Latins and Aristodemus of Cumae (504); survivors found refuge at Rome, origin of the Vicus Tuscus.

people.name: Thefarie Velianas
people.summary: Ruler of Caere (zilath or 'king' in the Phoenician text) who around 500 dedicated a sanctuary at Pyrgi to Uni-Astarte, recorded on the bilingual gold tablets found in 1964.

people.name: Lucius Sicinius Vellutus
people.summary: Leader of the First Secession who urged the plebs to the Mons Sacer and was among the first tribunes elected (493); Dionysius makes him prosecutor of Coriolanus.

people.name: Publius Licinius Calvus
people.summary: First plebeian elected military tribune with consular power (400); elected again in 396, he yielded his place to his son.

people.name: Lucius Genucius Aventinensis
people.summary: Second plebeian consul (365) and consul again in 362, the first plebeian consul to make war under his own auspices; he was ambushed and killed by the Hernici.
people.death: killed in battle with the Hernici

people.name: Gaius Poetelius Libo Visolus
people.summary: Tribune of the plebs 358 who carried the first law against canvassing, plebeian consul 360, 346 and 326, triumphing over the Gauls and Tiburtines (360); the abolition of nexum (lex Poetelia Papiria, 326) bears his name.

people.name: Gaius Maenius
people.summary: Plebeian consul 338 who defeated the Latins and Antiates at the Astura and fixed the beaks of Antium's ships to the speakers' platform; honoured with the Maenian column; censor 318 (balconies called maeniana) and dictator 320 and 314, when he investigated the Capuan conspiracy.

people.name: Titus Veturius Calvinus
people.summary: Consul 334 and 321, colleague of Sp. Postumius in the Caudine Forks disaster, and one of the guarantors handed over to the Samnites in 320.

people.name: Gaius Plautius Venox
people.summary: Censor 312 with Appius Claudius, credited with finding the springs of the Aqua Appia (hence 'Venox', the vein-finder); he resigned when Appius refused to lay down office after eighteen months.

people.name: Quintus Marcius Tremulus
people.summary: Plebeian consul 306 and 288, who crushed the Hernican revolt and was honoured with an equestrian statue before the temple of Castor.

people.name: Herennius Pontius
people.summary: Aged father of Gavius Pontius who, asked how to treat the Roman army trapped at Caudium, advised either releasing it unharmed or killing every man, and warned that a middle course would make enemies without weakening them.
people.detail: Cicero says he conversed with Archytas of Tarentum and Plato, an anecdote showing Samnite elites in the Italiote intellectual world.

people.name: Ovius Paccius
people.summary: Aged Samnite priest who in 293 at Aquilonia administered the terrible oath of the 'linen legion', reading from an ancient linen book, by which Samnite nobles swore to fight to the death.

people.name: Verginia (wife of Volumnius)
people.summary: Patrician woman who in 296, excluded from the shrine of Pudicitia Patricia for marrying the plebeian consul L. Volumnius, founded a shrine of Pudicitia Plebeia in her house on the Vicus Longus.

people.name: Minucia
people.summary: Vestal suspected because of her dress and convicted on a slave's evidence of unchastity, she was buried alive at the Colline Gate in 337.

people.name: Lucius Albinius
people.summary: Plebeian who, fleeing Rome before the Gauls in 390, made his wife and children get down from his cart so that the Vestals and the sacred objects could ride to Caere.
people.detail: Valerius Maximus and Livy make him an exemplum of religious piety; Aristotle's 'Lucius' who saved Rome may be him.

people.name: Sthenius Statilius
people.summary: Lucanian leader who twice attacked Thurii in the 280s, provoking the Thurians' appeal to Rome and the tribune C. Aelius' measure against him.

people.name: Britomaris
people.summary: Senonian chief who, according to Appian, killed Roman envoys in 284 to avenge his father, killed in the fighting at Arretium; his act provoked Dolabella's destruction of the Senones.

people.name: Phintias
people.summary: Tyrant of Acragas in the 280s who styled himself king, destroyed Gela and moved its people to his new city of Phintias (Licata), and fought Hicetas of Syracuse; his coins bear his name and the portrait of Artemis.
